characters.name: Jayce
characters.description: 100% Heroism Rating: By Act 2, his achievements with Hextech have made him extremely popular in Piltover. Mel leverages his status as the city's "Golden Boy" to get him a seat on the Council. Acquired Situational Narcissism: While he's stillthe most upstanding member of the Councilafter getting a seat, his issues with going along with their corruption and the stress of dealing with Zaun's growing belligerence make him a lot more sour and callous. Action Politician: Jayce is an inventor and nascent politician, but whenVi convinces him to hit Silco's Shimmer manufacturing plant he personally leads the Enforcers with his freshly built hammer, and he handles himself pretty damn well for his first fight. Adaptational Backstory Change: There are a few discrepancies between Jayce's lore in the game and show:In the game, Jayce was sponsored by Clan Giopara. In the show, it was Caitlyn's family, the Kirammans.The game says he first met Viktor at a Progress Day party, while in the show it's shortly after his apartment blows up.The game never says anything about him inventing Hextech, even implying it was already a part of everyday life in Piltover by the time he made a name for himself. Him and Viktor revolutionizing it is a major plot point in the show.There's also Jayce's in-game mentor, Stanwick Piddidly. In the show he's some kind of historical figure associated with the founding of Piltover, not part of Jayce's life in any meaningful way — The show's Jayce can't even really remember anything about him off the top of his head. In the game, Jayce was sponsored by Clan Giopara. In the show, it was Caitlyn's family, the Kirammans.

characters.name: Viktor
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: Viktor is far from a pushover inLeague of Legends,but once the Viktor ofArcanecompletes his transformation into the Herald of the Arcane, he becomes arguably the single most powerful character in the entire series. In addition to his traditionaldeath beams, he also demonstrates some impressive healing abilities andsome kind of psychic connectiontohis "Hexcorized" followers. On top of all that,this version can evenfly. Adaptational Superpower Change: Game lore says Viktor simply replaced his organic parts with mechanical ones over time, eventually going as far as to operate on his own brain.His change in the show is more magical, brought on by a combination of the Hexcore, Shimmer, and runes cut into his skin mutating parts of him into some kind of organically-moving metal. The core itself has also morphed into something still metallic but increasingly organic-looking. Aside from allowing him to walk without his cane for a while, the earliest stages don't provide much of a benefit. However, as Viktor's connection to the Arcane grows dramatically after fully fusing with the Hexcore, he gradually becomes more and more powerful, to the point that eventually he can only be called aHumanoid Abominationwith downright cataclysmic abilities. Adaptational Villainy:Unlike his video game counterpart, this Viktor has no qualms about forcing the transformation on people who won't/can't consentnoteHedoesinitially swear to only evolve willing volunteers, but later changes his tune when Jayce refuses to help him. Here, he tells Singed to begin the process that turns everyone he helped into an arcane construct, and his end goal involves bringing his "Glorious Evolution" to all of Runeterra. Ambiguous Robots:Following Viktor's increasingly dramatic transformation from the Hexcore, it becomes just as increasingly difficult to tell what exactly he and his followers have become. He's visibly made of some kind of metal and has the traditionaldegradation of his emotion

characters.name: Mel
characters.description: Alliterative Name:MelMedarda is the only character in Season One to play this trope completely straight. Artists Are Attractive: She's an alluring woman and Episode 6 reveals her to be a skilled painter. Revealed in the reverse order of the usual, in that her beauty, power and intelligence are presented as attractive first while her art is revealed asHidden Depths. Attack Reflector:Mel's powers have a defensive edge to them, creating barriers that can block and reflect attacks. She uses them to reflect Maddie's bullet intended for Caitlyn back against Maddie herself, killing her. Barrier Warrior:Her magic manifests largely as barriers capable ofreflecting attacksand protecting herself and others from damage, manifesting the first time when Jinx attacked the Council. The Beautiful Elite: A few of the Councilors qualify, since they're fairly good-looking and have the most money and power out of everyone in Piltover, but Mel is the one we...see the most of.

characters.name: Heimerdinger
characters.description: Absent-Minded Professor: Downplayed: while Heimerdinger is generally pretty on-the-ball, he has an unfortunate tendency to see things through a ponderous or scientific lens which, combined with his inability to comprehend the viewpoints of more short-lived species, means that he often misses the forest for the trees. Adaptational Deviation: Unlike in the game, Heimerdinger is openly a Yordle, instead of hiding his nature behind a glamour. Though, admittedly, the game has been a bit unclear on this element in recent years. All for Nothing: He pushed Jayce to not unveil his latest inventions to the world, saying that it shouldn't be presented to the public until they're sure it can't be abused or weaponized. Jayce follows his advice despite his own misgivings, alienating himself from Mel and Viktor, and then Jinx steals it and weaponizes it anyway. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: A variation.Being dropped into a different universe 3 years into the past, he took advantage of the lessons he'd learned in exile and used his influence as the Academy Dean and Head Councilor to better the conditions of Piltover and Zaun, rather than repeat his mistake of letting them fester in the main timeline. Authority in Name Only: Despite being officially the head of the Council, his one vote carries the exact same weight as any other member. Combined with his total lack of political acumen, Mel easily has more actual influence on the direction the council goes.

characters.name: Ambessa
characters.description: Abusive Parents: In the past, she once shamed her daughter for refusing to kill a captive princess and then killed said captive right in front of her, and Mel is still tormented by the princess' death years afterwards. She also eventually exiled Mel to Piltover, though this was the result of Ambessabeing weakened by her daughter's disapprovaland anearnest attempt to protect her from the Black Rose. Action Mom: Mother of Mel and Kino, and a ferocious Noxian warrior with many won battles behind her belt. Admiring the Abomination:Despite Warwick taking the lives of many of her soldiers and injuring Ambessa, she is more amazed by his destructive power than upset over her losses. She later negotiates a deal with Singed to grant her weapons such as him in exchange for anything he desires.After fully throwing in her lot with Viktor, she is in absolute awe of his powers and the inhuman monstrosities he makes of his former human followers, claiming that she now finally has the power to defeat her enemies. Mel, by comparison, is horrified and expresses her mother has lost her mind. Despite Warwick taking the lives of many of her soldiers and injuring Ambessa, she is more amazed by his destructive power than upset over her losses. She later negotiates a deal with Singed to grant her weapons such as him in exchange for anything he desires. After fully throwing in her lot with Viktor, she is in absolute awe of his powers and the inhuman monstrosities he makes of his former human followers, claiming that she now finally has the power to defeat her enemies. Mel, by comparison, is horrified and expresses her mother has lost her mind.

characters.name: Mylo
characters.description: Ambiguously Brown: Mylo has deeply tanned skin. Annoying Younger Sibling: It's implied Mylo is the second youngest of Vander's children, after Powder. However, both Vi and, to a lesser extent, Claggor, each make fun of Mylo for his less than pleasing traits. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!:Played for Laughswhen he finds a nose hair trimmer in Jayce's office and starts using it during the mission. Big Brother Bully: Spends a lot of his screentime belittling Powder for not being able to keep up and is the one to start calling her a jinx.He never gets a scene to show he cares about her before he dies and Jinx's paranoid, negative thoughts come in the form of him.Avertedin the alternate timeline where he does live, as Mylo is much nicer to Powder when they’re both adults. Big Ol' Eyebrows: His thick eyebrows are his most prominent feature.

characters.name: Claggor
characters.description: Acrofatic: Much more heavyset than his siblings but surprisingly agile. Ambiguously Related: Shares a similar physical resemblance to Vander: both have bulky physiques, brown hair and blue eyes. However, it's left unclear whether or not Claggor is his biological son, and Vander doesn't treat him any differently than the others. Badass Pacifist: Not unlike Vander, he'd rather keep him and his siblings out of trouble and doesn't directly seek confrontation. But when he has to fight, he clearly overpowers his foes, as Deckard and his gang can attest. Beware the Nice Ones: While usually pretty mellow, he can lay a hard beatdown on anyone who threatens his loved ones, as seen when he takes out some of Deckard's lackeys. Big Brother Bully: Downplayed. While he is the most pleasant among Vi and her siblings, he enjoys making jabs at Mylo from time to time, such as smacking his head during their heist or making fun of him at the arcade.

characters.name: Babette
characters.description: Chubby Chaser: Downplayed. She shows interest in Claggor, but moves on quickly when he ignores her. Dirty Old Woman: Implied. She made googly-eyes to Claggor, a teenage boy, much to his own discomfort. Early-Bird Cameo: She appears briefly in the first episode before having a speaking role in episode 5. Fan Disservice: She is an aging Yordle prostitute. Hooker with a Heart of Gold: She is a hooker that was a friend of Vander and is helpful towards Vi. In Act 2, she's become a Madame and is willing to update Vi about what's happened since Silco's rise despite the risk. Notably, she doesn't sell Vi outunlike another old friend of Vander.

characters.name: Felicia
characters.description: Best Friend: To Vander and Silco, to the point that they were the first people she told about her pregnancy since she was too nervous to tell her husband. Death by Origin Story: The very first scene of the series involves Vi and Powder seeing their parents' bodies among the casualties on the bridge. Season 2 pushes this further whenWarwick gets reminded of his past as Vander, and it's revealed he was a close friend of Felicia in his youth and her death led to his falling out with Silco. Deceased Parents Are the Best: While they were poor as most Zaunites were, it's obvious that she and her husband Connell raised Violet and Powder with love and affection before their untimely deaths. Even Jinx, unstable as she currently is, still loves them dearly and thinks fondly on what little she remembers of her parents. Dies Wide Open: When Vi and Powder find her body, her eyes are still opened. The Lost Lenore: A platonic version. Her death completely broke Vander, causing him to call off his revolution and subsequently try to murder Silco. In an unsent letter to Silco, Vander deeply regrets what he did to him and says Felicia's death made him lose his head.

characters.name: Huck
characters.description: Addled Addict: He's more well-put-together than others who have grown dependent on Shimmer, but he still craves it, especially when he sees Vi's medicine. Born Unlucky: Because of his scrawny and small stature, Huck is an easy target for ruffians to profit from, and leans on Vander for protection. After Vander dies and Silco takes over the city, he has no one else to stand up for him anymore and he turns to Shimmer, which mutated his body and made him addicted to the substance.Even when it seems like he's caught a break by Viktor healing him, it turns out to have had terrible side effects and he is eventuallyReforged into a Minion, with his empty body finally destroyed by Jayce and Mel. Body Horror: His head is covered in fleshy purple lumps as a result of his Shimmer addiction. Face–Heel Turn: He sells out Vi and Caitlyn to Silco himself for a vial of Shimmer, albeit with great shame and remorse. Geek Physiques: He is scrawny and isn't a threat to the people he made a deal with, which they counted on.

characters.name: Sevika
characters.description: Abnormal Limb Rotation Range: Downplayed. Sevika's first mechanical arm moves like a regular limb for the most part, not bending or rotating any differently than her flesh and blood arm. However, when Vi meets her after the time skip and pins her arm behind her, Sevika's able to twist it out of Vi's hold in a way that a normal arm could not. Achilles' Heel: A strangely specific one, but malfunctioning Hextech. It's implied that when Powder blew up the cannery with her Hextech monkey bomb, Sevika's body was contaminated by some lingering Hex Crystal dust or residue when she sustained her grievous injuries, which is the cause of the silvery-blue scars she has on her face in the present. While they normally are just scars that don't impede her,the Wild Rune exerting its power in the middle of her and Jinx's fight with Vi and Caitlyn causes all nearby Hextech to start going haywire; while Vi and Caitlyn aren't affected at all by their weaponry going on the fritz, Sevika instead gets functionallyelectrocutedby the latter's rifle when it comes into contact with her because of the residual Hex Crystals inside her body, allowing Caitlyn to overpower her during their fight. Absurdly Sharp Claws: The fingers of her mechanical arm end in razor-sharp claws, which she uses toimpale Vi and nearly kill her.The upgraded version that Jinx creates for her swaps the claws and fingers for a pair of metallicjawsthat are still just as sharp. Amazonian Beauty: Tall, dark-haired, muscular, and definitely not bad-looking. She's also a regular at Babette's brothel, which indicates Sevika has her admirers. Ambiguously Brown: She's dark-skinned, but her actual ethnicity has not yet been specified. Her name Sevika is a play on the Sanskrit word "sevikā", which may indicate Indian origins. The song which plays during her battle against Smeech and his goons alongside Jinx in Season 2,"Renegade (We Never Run)", implements some Indian vocalizations and instruments like tablas and sitars, references

characters.name: Deckard
characters.description: Addled Addict: One use of Shimmer leaves Deckard a weakened and shivering wreck once it wears off. He can barely stand up straight and is desperate for another dose when Silco offers it to him. Alas, Poor Villain: Despite his crimes, he was just a Zaunite kid who was manipulated by Silco into destroying his own physical and mental integrity by taking a powerful drug and becoming hopelessly addicted to it. At this point,his death at Vander's hands comes off as more of aMercy Killconsideringwhat Shimmer does to your body after the effects wear off. Ax-Crazy: Downplayed. Despite the implications of his intensely heightened aggression and bestial demeanor, Deckard does not entirely lose rationality under the effects of Shimmer. He is fully capable of restraint, following orders, and distinguishing friend from foe. However, he can be blindly aggressive to the point of attacking a fellow thug in his way of Vi. Brain in a Jar: Disturbingly, it's revealed in Season 2that after Deckard's death at the hands of Vander, Singed cut off his head to experiment with his Shimmer-addled brain. When Ambessa and Caitlyn tour Singed's lab during negotiations with him, they both take glances at Deckard's head in a jar with his brain exposed and lodged with syringes. The Brute: Silco deems Deckard incompetent after falling short to Vi and her friends, and thus has him instead serve as his main form of muscle after taking Shimmer.

characters.name: Thieram
characters.description: Back for the Finale:Thieram is one of the many Zaunites that take a final stand against the Noxian invaders in the series finale. Butt-Monkey: After barely answering her questions, Jinx pulls a prank on an already-terrified Thieram by planting a paint bomb on his back. Later on, Vi suddenly attacks The Last Drop on a quiet day and he can only duck down behind the counter and exit unseen. Cannot Talk to Women: Although he's a mess around Jinx due to beingThe Dreaded, she's also a pretty girl who acts flirty with him, which makes him all the more nervous around her. Minion with an F in Evil: Although he tries to be intimidating when it's necessary to guard his post, he's a stuttering wreck when confronted with any real danger, a far cry from Silco's average goons. Although considering said danger isJinxand thenVi, it's hard to really blame him. Nervous Wreck: He is completely terrified when Jinx stops by for a drink and is unable to coherently answer any of her questions.

characters.name: Gustove
characters.description: All There in the Manual: The official name used for him by the writers in Season 1 was just "Burly Henchman", and in the liveArcane: Enter the Undercityproduction, he was called Lock. The "Nothing to Lose" preview clip for Season 2 finally revealed his name to be Gustove Jowler, also known as "The Scowler" in pit fights. Awesome McCoolname: Gustove "The Scowler" Jowler has a nice ring to it. Bald of Evil: He's bald and a henchman of Silco. Boxing Battler: By Season 2, he's a butterfly-weight Piltover Boxing League champion, although he gets knocked out by Vi with a single uppercut before he can be seen in action. Blood from the Mouth: Gets this after Vi clocks him with Vander's iron gauntlets. Happens once again when she knocks his lower jaw prosthesis off with an uppercut in Season 2.

characters.name: Ran
characters.description: One of Silco's underlings. Affably Evil: She silently greets Marcus with a wave and (somewhat flirty) smile when he sees her and Silco in his daughter's room. All There in the Manual: Her name and pronouns (she/they) were first revealed on Twitter by a pair of the writers. Artificial Limbs: She has what looks like mechanical fingers on their right hand. The entire hand could be a replacement, but it's hard to tell. Regardless, the replacement happened after theTime Skipfor an unknown reason. Back for the Finale: Ran appears in the final episode of the series,on the frontlines with numerous other Zaunites taking a final stand against the Noxians.

characters.name: In General
characters.description: Dead Alternate Counterpart: In this timeline, Vi died in the explosion at Jayce's apartment. It's also implied that Viktor (since Hextech was never invented to cure him) and Jayce (who was only notDriven to Suicideafter the explosion because of the hope of developing Hextech) are also dead. Death of a Child: Vi died as a teenager, and her death caused the two cities to make amends and thrive in peace. Everybody Lives: Notably, just about everyone of particular note from the main timeline who perished are instead alive and well in this one, living together happily and peacefully in a unified Piltover and Zaun, with the sole exception being Vi. Everyone Has Standards:Marcusand another Enforcer who walked into Jayce's apartment after the explosion are horrified to see that Vi, a young girl, died as a consequence of the explosion. It's implied that Marcus was much more lenient on the young Zaun thieves as a result. Formerly Fat: Claggor is more stocky than rotund in his adulthood.

characters.name: Finn
characters.description: Aesop Amnesia: He is clearly more bark than bite, and is forced toplea Silco for his lifewhen the latter makes him remember who's boss. Instead of learning his lesson, Finnstillattempts tooverthrow Silco as Chief Chem-Baron,which costs him his life when Sevika killshim, and was never planning to work for "a worm like him". Ain't Too Proud to Beg: When Silco decides to discipline his disgruntled Chem-Baron associates by suffocating them with a particular toxin, Finn boldly stands up to his face and refuses to back down. However, after enough of taking the air in, he's reduced to desperately begging for his life and is completely humiliated by Silco. Asshole Victim:Finn is suddenly betrayed and killed off by Sevika in a second attempt at betraying Silco, and she outright calls him a worm after killing him. Considering what a smug and conniving thug he presented himself as, there's not much sympathy to be had. Big Bad Wannabe: He becomes an antagonist for Silco in the final arc of Season 1, seeking to depose him as leader of the Chem-Barons. However, while he puts up the image of a smooth-talkingChessmaster, Finn is out of his league whenever he tries making a move. The first time he directly questions Silco's leadership, he's left humiliated when introduced to polluted air from the mines. His second attempt appears on track for success when he tries recruiting Sevika to his side, but she opts to remain loyal to Silco and slashes Finn's throat at the moment of his coup. He spends his final moments choking on his own blood before dying pathetically. Black and Yellow and Alarming All Over: Not that his obscenely loud yellow jacket makes him any more threatening.

characters.name: Smeech
characters.description: Alien Blood:Subverted. Heseemsto bleed bright green,and Sevika is coated in bright green liquid after killing him, but it's actually just from the Chemtech powering hisArtificial Limbs. Artificial Limbs: All of Smeech's limbs are mechanical. The writersstatethat it was his people that made Sevika's arm, and Season 2 reveals that they're packing all sorts of weapons for combat. Ascended Extra: He only had one minor appearance and no speaking lines in Season 1, but in Season 2, he gains speaking lines and serves as a minor antagonist, wanting to deliver Jinx alive to Piltover forblowing up the council. Bad Boss: Smeech is shown to treat his accountant horrifically, constantly demeaning him and even forcing him to risk his life at one point when Smeech himself is capable and always ready for danger. Big Bad Wannabe: Thinks he can gain favor with Piltover and therefore obtain much more power by capturing Jinx.She and Sevika make him pay dearly - and fatally - for his ambitions in the first and only episode he's a major character in.

characters.name: Madam Margot
characters.description: Adaptation Dye-Job: She's a blond in the series, but theUnder The Undercityevents give her silver-colored hair instead. Alliterative Name:MadamMargot. All There in the Manual: According to theEnter the Undercityevent, she's the Madame of Zaun's entire prostitution ring, with her enterprise having the name of "Vyx". Her name was also revealed to be "Madam Margot". Advertised Extra: Appeared in only one scene in the previous season, and the trailer featured a statue of Margot's head emitting smoke, hinting at a more important role. Margot only gets one significant speaking scene beforeshe arrested by Caitlyn and her strike team during a musical montage in "Finally Got The Name Right"and is never seen again. The Baroness: A beautiful self-made woman who owns a prostitution ring.

characters.name: Chross
characters.description: Evil Cripple: Chross sits in a wheelchair, likely because of his advanced age. It's easier to see in concept art, but eagle eyed viewers can see that his chair is different from the one's the other Chem-Barons use. Four Eyes, Zero Soul: He wears round sunglasses, and it a corrupted criminal capturing children for his own agenda. The Informant: He specializes in selling information across Zaun. The Spymaster: His company works in surveillance, providing secrets and vast amounts of information for Silco's operations. Suddenly Voiced: Like the other Chem-Barons, he doesn't speak in the first season, but does in Season 2.

characters.name: Singed
characters.description: Adaptational Deviation: In the original lore, Singed was outcast from Piltover due to his hatred of Hextech and going bankrupt from his alchemic research no longer being funded by sponsors. Due to the massive retcon with the time period and Hextech's discovery, Singed is instead suggested to only have fallen out of favor due to his unethical research. He also has no problems with working with Hextech, being fascinated by Viktor's Hex Core and Jinx suggesting the Hextech Gem she stole be given to him for research. On another note,Arcanenow explicitly stateshis true identity is none other than Corin Reveck,Orianna'sfather, despite Singed and Orianna's father previously being two distinct characters. Adaptational Sympathy: BeforeArcane, Singed was completely devoid of sympathetic qualities. Here, it's shown he had more benevolent intentions in the past, and is even compassionate with Silco over being a parent, since "he too once had a daughter".Taken further in Season 2, as it's revealed his entire motive is to save his daughter from death. It also doubles as aPlayed Withexample; while the greater sympathy makes him more understandable than his game counterpart, it also makes how appallingly cruel to others he is much more noticeable compared to his rather one-noteCard-Carrying Villainpersonality in the games, especially when it comes to his musings on the need to break Vander completely to make Warwick loyal to him and Ambessa. Adaptational Villainy: By virtue of being aComposite Character,Corin Reveck, Orianna's father, was originally written as a well-meaning toymaker who only relocated to Zaun to secure enough money to help treat his daughter's condition, but showed no signs of ever being a malicious person. However, his new identity as Singed in this seriesturns his noble motivation of trying to save his daughter into a crux of diving off into worsening amoral behavioras he helped create a druglike substance so dangerously mutagenic that it has ruined countless li

characters.name: Rio
characters.description: A strange creature dying of terminal illness, introduced in a flashback that details Viktor's first meeting with Singed. Ambiguous Situation: It's not clear what exactly Rio is supposed to be. Viktor is clearly unfamiliar with what she is, while Singed calls her a "mutation" without further explanation. The presence of a "Rio" Pixiemander inTeamfight Tacticssuggests she may be a mutated Waverider, a creature fromLegends of Runeterrathat the Pixiemander Little Legend is based on. And I Must Scream: It's made painfully and horrifically clear that Singed's method of preserving her life is causing her unimaginable pain. Cute Monster: Despite being an alien-like salamander on death's door, her large eyes make her darn cute. No wonder why young Viktor quickly offers to help Singed save her life. Fate Worse than Death: Viktor eventually believes the means Singed uses to prolong her life to be too inhumane, preferring her to be put out of her misery. Singed refuses and keeps her around even today, where she's barely recognizable from her old form.

characters.name: Scar
characters.description: Bat People: Scar has grey fur, a snout-like nose, huge ears and fangs, although he has arms instead of wings. Beast Man: Scar is a Chirean, a species that resembles a humanoid bat. The Big Guy: He's noticeably taller than most of the other characters, and is one of the Firelight's most prominent fighters. Commonality Connection: With Sevika, ironically, given their history. Both are second-in-command to the closest things Zaun has to centralized authority, and are forced to assume leadership after the sudden loss of their leaders, andthe two of them jointly represent Zaun at Jayce's war council. Good Is Not Soft: Was ready tomurder Vi with a spear(whom he assume was working withJinx) if not from his leader stopping him.

characters.name: Janna
characters.description: Adaptational Modesty: Has short sleeves and shoulder covers that tone down her skimpiness from her base look in the game. All There in the Manual: Her true name is only mentioned in the description for "To Ashes and Blood", which also provides the translation for the Shumiran chants used in the song. Blow You Away: Janna is said to be a wind spirit who uses her powers to help Zaunites breathe. The Ghost: There are a few artistic depictions of her, but she doesn't appear in person. Maybe Magic, Maybe Mundane: Jinx posits that stories of Janna rescuing miners could have been hallucinations induced by oxygen deprivation.

characters.name: Deckard's Gang
characters.description: Bald of Evil: One of them is bald. Jerkass: Unlike Deckard, there's nothing charismatic to them, and the bald one seems almost sadistic to attack the group.Thug 1:[with a smirk] You hear that, Deckard? "They don't want any trouble". Karma Houdini Warranty: The brunet causes Powder to lose the Piltover supplies and escapes being beaten up. When we see him again after theTime Skip, he's become addicted to Shimmer like Deckard was, his body having been hopelessly mutated. Nasal Trauma: One of them has a broken nose, and Mylo and Vi break it again on two different instances during their fight, with Vi even striking it with a plank. By the time we see him again after theTime Skip, he now has a prosthetic nose. Sand in My Eyes: How Claggor defeats the blond.

characters.name: Shoola
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Compared to the other councilors Shoola had the least amount of characterization in season one, but in the first act of season 2 she shoots up in importance. With Jayce no longer participating in Council affairs and three councilors dead, she becomes the deciding vote between Salo and Mel's plans. Salo wants to storm the undercity while Mel wants a more restrained response, and ultimately it's up to Shoola who gets their way—at least until Ambessa takes over through Caitlyn as her puppet. Bald of Authority: A female example; Shoola is a bald woman in a position of power. Black Boss Lady: Along with Mel among the Piltover Council. Cool Mask: In the second season she wears a golden mask over the burns she sustained in Jinx's rocket attack. Facial Horror: After the attack on the council, most of the skin around Shoola's right eye has beenblasted off, leaving her flesh exposed. Shoola later wears a golden mask around that eye to hide her injury.

characters.name: Bolbok
characters.description: Asshole Victim: He's one of the most openly hostile concilors towards Zaunites,and one of the casulties in Jinx's attack on the Council at the beginning of Season 2. Horrible Judge of Character: Despite his disdain for the Undercity, he accepts the Enforcers' report that Silco is merely a honest businessman. He also entirely trustedMarcus. The Needless: Showrunner Christian Linkeconfirmedthat Bolbok does not need to eat. Off with His Head!:Jayce and Mel find him beheaded in the aftermath of Jinx's missile attack, and because he's a robot, it's aBloodless Carnage. Robotic Psychopath: Bolbok appears to be at least partially machine; he is also the outwardly coldest member of the council, being the one to push for Jayce's banishment and openly advocating for an uncompromising no-mercy policy towards the Undercity.

characters.name: Hoskel
characters.description: Asshole Victim: Among the most dishonest and corrupted in the Council,and one of the casulties in Jinx's attack on the Council at the beginning of Season 2. Bald of Evil: Balding and one of the most amoral councilors. Beard of Evil: He's got a beard and is the most openly hostile and prejudiced concilor. Fat Bastard: He's overweight and an elitist, condescending douchebag. Fat Idiot: Hoskel is short, fat, pompous, only concerned with profit, and very dim; hisEstablishing Character Momentsees Mel giving him a puzzle box for his birthday, claiming it's for "the sharpest minds" when in fact it's achildren's toy, only for Hoskel to be unable to solve it. In fact, he'sstillshown to be struggling with ityearslater in Act 2.

characters.name: Tobias Kiramman
characters.description: All There in the Manual: His first name was revealed by a writer from the show on Twitter. Beard of Sorrow:His facial hair becomes longer and more unkempt after the death of his wife. Good Parents: Cassandra is a case ofParents as People, whilst Tobias's relationship with Caitlyn is much warmer. Happily Married: Appears to be the case with Cassandra. Hidden Depths: Tobias has some degree of medical experience. When an injured Caitlyn returns home, he takes out his kit and removes the shrapnel from her leg.

characters.name: Ximena Talis
characters.description: All for Nothing: Subverted at the last second. Her efforts to save Jayce from banishment by breaking his heart leads to him attempting suicide. Had Viktor not intervened, her sacrifice would've all been for naught. Artificial Limbs: Two of her fingers are mechanical after losing them to a frostbite. Back for the Finale: After being absent for the entirety of the second season, she briefly appears in the final episode,mourning the loss of her son. Break His Heart to Save Him: In order to save her son from banishment after he's caught meddling with magic, shetells the council that he's not right in the head, which breaks his heart. Broken Pedestal: While Jayce is grateful for her saving him from banishment, he's also incredibly betrayed when she essentially sabotages his attempts to harness magic by making him out to look insane in the eyes of the council. He attempts suicide shortly thereafter, implying that he was fine with making her efforts to save him meaningless.

characters.name: Marcus
characters.description: Anti-Villain: He doesn't want to be corrupt, but he's forced to make deals with Silco and lacks the courage to do anything meaningful about it. By Act III, Silco is now threatening his daughter's life if he doesn'tkill Caitlyin and retrieve the hextech crystal. An Arm and a Leg:Jinx's bomb blows one of his arms clean off. He dies from shock and blood loss a few seconds later. Alas, Poor Villain:Despite being aDirty Copwho tried to kill Caitlyin and Ekko, his death is painted in a somber light, and Caitlyn retroactively suggests to the Council that Silco had leverage over him to make him do what he did. He also leaves his daughter Ren an orphan. Apologetic Attacker:While he has zero hesitation in gunning down Ekko, he is greatly reluctant to murder Caitlyn, grimacing and shaking while holding her at gunpoint. Beard of Sorrow: After the time skip, he gains a noticeable pencil stache that emphasizes how deeply uncomfortable he is with his lot in life.

characters.name: Grayson
characters.description: Affably Evil: Shares a drink with Vander while politely forcing him to give up one of his people to take the fall for the bombing at Piltover. Anti-Villain: While she's an antagonistic force, she's mostly reasonable and willing to make deals under the table for the greater good. Big Good: She's this as the Sheriff of the Enforcers, and Piltover's unofficial liaison to Zaun as a whole. While she makes deals with Vander under the table, she's ultimately working together to minimize conflict and loss of life for both sides, in stark contrast to the other Enforcers or Council members who treat Zaunites with either total apathy or contempt. Part of her initial refusal to arrest Vander is out of fear of the chaos it would incite in the undercity.It's no coincidence that after she's murdered, the Enforcers quickly become even more corrupt and ineffectual under Marcus' leadership. Contralto of Strength: She's the head Enforcer, and is played by Shohreh Aghdashloo, who is known for her rather deep and raspy voice. Da Chief: She serves as this to the Enforcers, having to deal with Marcus' corruption and the moreCowboy Coptendencies of the Enforcers under her.

characters.name: Loris
characters.description: The Alcoholic: He's introduced passed out under some newspapers next to a small collection of bottles, and he carries a flask on his person that he offers to Vi shortly after meeting her. Back for the Dead:After skipping most of Acts 2, he finally returns in final two episodes. He is killed in series finale by an arrow to the neck. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: When he's introduced, it's as drunkard who was sleeping under some newspapers when Vi accidentally hits him with a bottle, who talks Vi into drinking with him and then accompanies her to the Piltover memorial service. When Renni attacks the ceremony, he proves to be a surprisingly competent Enforcer, grabbing a shield and managing to hold off a Chemtank-empowered thug with nothing but his own strength, and Caitlyn grants him a spot in her strike team afterwards.He is also the only person outside of Mel to see immediately throughallof Ambessa's tricks and understands well enough what she's trying to do, and wants no part in the police state she's trying to turn Piltover into to suit her interests. Damager, Healer, Tank: He's the Tank of the team, wielding a shield and effectivelybeingone to rest of the Strike Force. Everyone Has Standards: Loris is a generally friendly guy who, despite being willing to be part of a strike force that employs somenastyshock and awe tactics against the people of Zaun, is trying to do the right thing by bringing Jinx to justice when it is clear that the conflict with Zaun is getting out of hand. However, he draws the line atbecoming part of what is essentiallya fascist statethe moment he recognizes what Ambessa is trying to do, and when Caitlyn falls to the temptation to declare martial law,Loris quietly checks out altogether.

characters.name: Steb
characters.description: All There in the Manual: He's never called by his name in the show proper, only promotional material refer to him as "Steb". Damager, Healer, Tank: The healer, being the one to inspect hostages after fights. He is often seen using a light to check eyesight in particular. Determinator: Steb is quick to act no matter the odds - attacking a Chemtank with an axe to save Maddie, andimmediately taking over to arm the bomb in Ep 9 when the original carrier is killed. This is despite having his gasmask ripped off, exposing him to the weaponised Grey. Later, he is immediately up and fighting the Noxians again when Jinx distracts them long enough for the captured enforcers to grab their weapons. Deus Ax Machina: Uses one to injure Chemtank-using thug's leg when he's about to kill Maddie during Renni's raid. Expressive Ears: It's subtle, but his pointed ears move - e.g. flicking when he notices the approaching Zaunites on the bridge, and pinning back against his head in distress whenthe enforcers are betrayed and captured in episode 9.

characters.name: The Warden
characters.description: The warden of Stillwater Hold. Always a Bigger Fish: He'sLarge and in Chargeof Stillwater, but his size means nothing toWarwick, who easily disposed of him during his rampage. Asshole Victim: Ahugeasshole wardenwho got his comeuppance by Warwick's claws. Back for the Dead: Returns in Season 2,only to be killed offscreen by Warwick during his rampage at Stillwater. Deadpan Snarker: Speaks in a disinterested, ironic tone of voice, and seems to have a wicked sense of humor.Caitlyn: How many... "talks"notea.k.a beatingsdid you have with [Vi]?Warden: You know... I never even thought to count.

characters.name: Elora
characters.description: The Confidant: Before she met Jayce, Elora was the only person Mel would trust with her concerns and plans. The Consigliere: She's Mel Medarda's most trusted advisor. Cruel and Unusual Death:The Black Rose uses chains with thorns toinvade her eyes and mouth, before proceeding to tear her body apart. Disposable Woman:She ends up getting killed before Mel's eyes by the Black Rose as she's being captured. Dropped a Bridge on Her: Has been a loyal friend and assistant of Mel since the first season,only to be brutally murdered byLeBlancin cold blood for no other reason than to hurt Mel.

characters.name: Ren
characters.description: Marcus' young daughter. Children Are Innocent: She's happy to let Silco wait for her father in her home, even building a card castle with him. She doesn't knowwhat kind of man he is, but her fatherdoesand is terrified at the implications of Silco's presence in his home. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She doesn't appear in Season 2, after Season 1 leaves her whereabouts unknownfollowing the death of her father. The Cutie: An adorable little girl withlarge grey eyesandYouthful Frecklesfor extra cuteness factor. Daddy's Girl: Shown to be close to her father.

characters.name: Lest
characters.description: Cat Folk: She's some kind of feline vastaya; not only does she have large ears on top of her head and a bushy tail, she has a catlike nose anddigitigradelegs. Furry Confusion: She uses the expression "like a cat backed into a corner" despite being a catwoman herself. Judging by Mel's brief smirk, it might be an intentional joke. The Informant: She works at a drug den Salo frequents, and provides Mel with any information she happens to overhear from him. Or with evidence of his drug use she can use to discredit him. Mistaken for Prostitute: She quickly hides her Shimmer equipment when she hears Ambessa about to enter Salo's room, but then the latter sees her kneeling in front of a half-naked Salo, bringing this trope to mind. It thankfully avoids Ambessa from getting suspicious of Lest. Not What It Looks Like: As she applies Shimmer on Salo's injuries, she overhears Ambessa coming by and quickly puts aways her equipment. When Ambessa walks in, the drugs are hidden, but Lest is kneeling in front of Salo, who's laying on the couch with only his underwear on (making it seem like she was about to go down on him). There's an awkward moment of silence before Ambessa tells her to leave.

characters.name: Rictus
characters.description: Always a Bigger Fish: He's an absolute giant and easily overpowers his opponents. Against Warwick, however? His size meansnothing,and he gets easily killed as a result. Anti-Magic: Manages to break free fromAmara'sblood magic through the runes on his weapon, and is later able to use it to block Jinx's blasts of Hextech magic from Zapper. This is also anEaster Eggreferencing the Kaenic Rookern item from theLeague of Legendsgame. Asshole Victim: As Ambessa's chief enforcer, Rictus oversaw the brutality of Piltover's martial law over Zaun. He personally had various Zaunites unjustly imprisoned and beat some to a pulp with his bare hands. As a result,anyone but Ambessa will find it difficult to grieve his gruesome death by Warwick. Beard of Barbarism:Downplayed. While Noxians are not barbaric, they are considerably more martial then Piltover or Zaun and he sports one of the most impressive beards of the series. Bodyguarding a Badass: He's frequently shown guarding Ambessa, and even helps distract aBlack Rose assassinfrom killing her, but Ambessa herself is perfectly capable of holding her own in combat.

characters.name: Ta'Fik
characters.description: The Heavy: Although he's not the ultimate mastermind behind the villains inChosen of the Wolf, he's nonetheless the main antagonist, being Ambessa's opponent for the throne of House Medarda and the chief tool of the Black Rose's plots. Hypocrite: He accuses Ambessa of being a kinslayer who poisoned their dying grandfather before he could appoint Ta'Fik to the throne, despite himself being responsible for the battle that fatally wounded him. Unwitting Pawn: Ta'Fik thinks he's leading his house to greatness, unaware all the while he's merely leading the Medardas to being another weapon inLeblanc'sarsenal.

characters.name: Rell
characters.description: Adaptational Backstory Change: Rell was originally sold to the Black Rose as a young child and tortured in their "care" by her own mother.Chosen of the Wolfdepicts her as only falling into their clutches as a teenager, with her parents merely being emotionally neglectful and exploitative of her success in the gladiator pits rather than outright monsters. Adopt-a-Prodigy: Ambessa takes a liking to her because of her strength, intelligence, and mage powers, which she thinks would make her an exceptionally useful ally to Mel that would make up for her biological daughter's perceived weakness. Adopted into Royalty: Ambessa tries to adopt her into House Medarda, but Rell is sadly kidnapped soon after to be turned into a slave of the Black Rose. Age Lift: She's a teenager inLeaguecanon, but is made the same age is Mel inArcane's universe, meaning she should be an adult in the present.

characters.name: The Illusionary Sorceress
characters.description: Adaptational Modesty: In her undisguised appearance,LeBlancwears a far more conservative black gown that covers her whole body (including most of her face) than her StripperificMs. Fanservicedesign from any other media — but given how it is all but flat out stated she is operating through adoppelgangerper her usual modus operandi, it is not established if this is a definitive new look forLeBlancor just another form she's assuming at the time. Big Bad: Although she seldom appears,LeBlancis the primary source of conflict in Ambessa's prequel novel,Chosen of the Wolf. Not only is she propping up the matriarch's cousin Ta'Fik as aPuppet King, but she also has Ambessa's husband killed, kidnaps Rell from her care, and is ordering the experiments on young mages, which spurns Mel's father to abandon the Black Rose and help Ambessa to protect their daughter from the pale woman's grasp. Chain Pain: Within her own world,LeBlanc'sprimary means of dealing with any opposition is to wrap, bind, or shred them with thorny, red-black chains made of magic. Curb-Stomp Battle: The only thing that was stoppingLeBlancwere the anti-magic runes Ambessa wore on her arms. Once Caitlyn rips those off,LeBlancutterlythrashesAmbessa with ease the moment Mel calls on her. Didn't See That Coming: Mel ends up pulling one over her in the fight against Ambessa by calling on her to trap her mother. While she initially takes this as a sign Mel is willing to join her and gladly deals Ambessa mortal injuries within her domain, she doesn't account for Mel herself invading her realm and banishing her right after, allowing her mother a more peaceful death in her arms while making it clear to the Deceiver that she's now out to settle the score for her family's sake.

characters.name: The Mysterious Mage
characters.description: An unknown mage wandering on his own who saves Jayce and his mother who were about to die from a harsh blizzard in a snowy region and gives Jayce a magic crystal. Ambiguously Human: He presumably seems like a human but considering he's from a world where other fantasy creatures exist and the fact he's untouched by the blizzard, it's possible he might be a completely different specimen. Big Damn Heroes: When all hope seems lost for a young Jayce and his mother, the mage appears out of the blue and teleports them to a safer location. Exposed to the Elements: He seems to be the least affected in the snowstorm (presumably from using magic) unlike Jayce and his mother who were about to die from it. The Faceless: His face is obscured making his identity unknown.

characters.name: (Alternate) Powder
characters.description: Alternate Self: To Jinx. Here, she never became Jinx but lost Vi during the heist at Jayce's apartment, which didn't stop her from growing up into a sweet and brilliant young woman using her knowledge for good. Animal Motifs: Like in the main timeline, Powder is still associated with monkeys. In both universes, she's aGrease Monkey, and Powder owns severalCymbal-Banging Monkeysthat she integrates in Ekko's Z-Drive. But while Jinx's motif representsManiac Monkeysdue to her disturbed mental state, Powder is more of afunny monkey, presenting her as more leveled, positive and light-hearted compared to Jinx. Artists Are Attractive: Powder makes paintings in her spare time, and she grew up to be a beautiful young woman (who's healthier physically and mentally on top of avoiding becoming Jinx). Big Sister Worship: Like in the main universe, but here it takes a more tragic turn since Vi died young. Powder still looks back at the memory of Vi fondly, and is very touched when she sees the tribute Ekko painted for Vi (on the same mural used by the Firelights in his universe):Powder: [with melancholy] She looks so badass. Break the Cutie: In this universe, Powder had to witness Vi die in the explosion from Jayce's apartment, and cried her eyes out while holding her sister's lifeless body.
